Theorem
[Existence of finite-time singularity models] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0102 ↗ thm:chow-iii-no-local-collapsing ↗ prop:chow-iii-cgt-injectivity 1. ch19:19.4\group Singularity Models

Let $t_i\nearrow T$, $p_i\in M$, $r_i>0$, and $K_i=|\Rm |(p_i,t_i)\to \infty $ satisfy $|\Rm |(x,t)\le CK_i$ on $B_{g(t_i)}(p_i,r_i)$ for $t<t_i$ and $K_i r_i^2\to \infty $. A subsequence of $g_i(t)=K_i g(t_i+t/K_i)$ converges in the pointed smooth Cheeger--Gromov sense to a complete ancient solution with nonnegative scalar curvature which is $\kappa $-noncollapsed at all scales.
